The natural order is the Romans at the top, the slaves at the very bottom. And Jesus is saying, "No, it's the opposite. Slaves at the top, Romans at the bottom." Because the Romans are trapped and cursed by the evil in their hearts. Whereas the slaves are free and they can liberate everyone through their compassion, through their love, through their forgiveness.

That's why the Roman psalm is a threat. As we discussed last class, that's what Romans do. They do evil and then get Greeks or Jews to write the history to explain why it was good. So in other words, as I will discuss next class, the story of Christianity was invented by the Romans. Because this story conveniently excuses the Romans from all blame even though they killed Jesus. It puts all the blame on Jews.

Christianity is not an invention of Jesus but of the Romans. And that's something I'll show you next class. But are we clear before I go into the evidence?

The idea here is that if you read Homer, the Iliad, or Dante's Divine Comedy, you will see the divine spark reflected in you. These great books are a portal into the divine. The problem though is most people cannot read these texts. So the question then is what do common people do? Jesus is a portal into the vine right? If you just remember his life and recite his sayings, that will give you access to the vine and remind you of who you are.

So Jesus is really about democratizing the divine. He allows anyone to access the divine whereas before, you had to access it through poetry. The center of Jewish life is Jerusalem. In the center of Jerusalem is a temple rebuilt under Herod. We know that Jesus was born in Galilee, which is cosmopolitan because it's by the coast and experiences different religions and cultures.

The crucifixion of Jesus is brutal. After his death, many sects of Christianity believed different things and argued with each other until the Catholic Church won because they were run by the Roman Empire. In 1945 in Egypt, we discovered the gospel of Thomas, a major book that records what I believe are the true teachings of Jesus.

Let's first look at the true teachings of Jesus and then explain why I think this is actually his true teachings.
